cues.brief: heavy rain drumming on a corrugated tin awning, dense metallic patter, water pouring off the lip, heard from under or just outside it; steady; tin and water; close, slightly enclosed; wet, cosy-annoying. Full level, smears into S1 and is gone by the f50 cut.

the soi floor in heavy rain: rain hissing on wet concrete, the drip curtain splattering into a filling puddle (deep plops among the hiss), a gutter gurgling, no traffic, no voices, no thunder; steady 14 s loop; water on concrete and water; a narrow lane between low walls; wet, close. Full level with A1; smears into S1.

a thin high mosquito whine close to the ear (fundamental near 600 Hz, buzzy harmonics), slow doppler sways as it circles near an ankle, intermittent; 4 s loopable; wings; close, slightly dry under the rain; annoying, intimate. Centre-left, swaying; smears into S1.

flip-flops running on wet concrete through shallow water: rubber slaps and small splashes, footfalls on +4, +14, +24 (one file with three steps 10 f apart, or three hits); 1.2 s; rubber, water, concrete; close, outdoors; hurry

shrink: a fast pitch zip, the full-size rain and whine stretch and smear upward as she shrinks, ending in a soft round pop and a breath of air on the puff peak (+19), then the slowed world opens; 0.9 s; air, glassy smear; from close soi to vast; uncanny, "the world just got huge" (not a cartoon sparkle)

slowed giant rain: a low soft hush of air and every 1-2 s one deep, soft, distant boom of a huge drop landing far off (a slowed splash, low and round, long reverb tail), no patter, no hiss; 16 s loop; water mass and air; vast open space; the world slowed and enormous. Runs f50-f980: -6 dB under SH06, -30 dB over SH07 +0..+14, low-passed ~500 Hz and -4 dB in SH15, hard off at f980.

the same insect slowed to its own scale: a deep soft rhythmic thrum-thrum of large membranes at 1.3 strokes per second (locked to the drawn flap), each stroke an airy whoosh with a faint resonant low hum and a dry hinge tick; 6 s loop; membrane, air; close, huge; alive, slightly creepy. To her right; in SH04 it drops away with the mosquito +17..+31 falling slightly in pitch.
one low bowed double-bass note with a soft swell and a faint high air harmonic; 2.2 s; ominous but not horror; under "ฝนเม็ดใหญ่ที่สุด"
a vast mass of water descending overhead: a deep slow wobbling "wub... wub" of the water body oscillating, a soft low roar of air pushed ahead of it, growing; 3 s; water, air; close above, big; dread
the drop swallows the mosquito: a deep soft wet "gloomp", a huge water body swallowing something small, muffled, round, no crack, short wet tail; 0.6 s; water; close; surprising, not violent

W2 returns unbroken as the mosquito flies back up into frame (the joke), runs to f324 where W-HIT takes it out. the same insect slowed to its own scale: a deep soft rhythmic thrum-thrum of large membranes at 1.3 strokes per second (locked to the drawn flap), each stroke an airy whoosh with a faint resonant low hum and a dry hinge tick; 6 s loop; membrane, air; close, huge; alive, slightly creepy
